title: Measure precision for scanner evaluations
description:
Purpose: Collect the design for true precision of DataParade scanner evaluations. Recall-first Plexus evals treat each gold annotation as an Item and ask whether the scanner detected it. Precision is a different problem: every in-scope scanner finding must be judgeable as true or false positive. Do not implement under this initiative until the design is agreed.

Why it is separate:
- Recall only needs gold positives (and optional known negatives).
- Precision needs an exhaustive scope, or unmatched findings turned into items for adjudication.
- Plexus already reports binary precision with Yes as the positive class. That number is not meaningful for detections until the false-positive set exists.
- Mixing unfinished precision into the first recall evaluations would recreate vanity metrics.

Exclusions (until explicitly pulled into a later epic):
- Implementing precision in the first Plexus recall scorecard
- Rewriting the 150 proposed annotations to be exhaustive
- New detector families

Definition of Done for this planning initiative:
- Agreed definition of an in-scope finding
- Agreed way to produce judgeable false-positive candidates
- Agreed mapping onto Plexus Items / Evaluation so precision is comparable across runs
- Child epics/stories filed only after that agreement

This initiative stays in planning until those questions are answered.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text:
## Idea log (2026-08-27) — planning only

Recall-first Plexus path (not this initiative): each gold annotation is an Item; the scanner predicts Yes/No detected; evaluation is recall.

Precision is the dual: among findings the scanner emitted in scope, how many were real.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  gold[Gold positives] --> recallEval[Recall eval]
  scanner[Scanner findings] --> inScope[In-scope findings]
  gold --> match[Location match]
  inScope --> match
  match -->|unmatched finding| fpCandidate[FP candidate item]
  match -->|matched gold| tp[True positive]
  fpCandidate --> adjudicate[Human accept or reject]
  adjudicate --> precisionEval[Precision eval]
```

Open questions to collect here:

1. **What is in-scope?** Manifest `scope.include` files only? Exhaustive review of those files (corpus skill already requires this for true precision)? Language-unread files excluded so unread does not look like a false negative *or* a false positive?

2. **How do FP candidates become Items?** After a scan, every in-scope finding that does not overlap gold becomes an Item with ground truth unknown until adjudication. That is a dataset-curation loop, not a metric formula.

3. **Plexus mapping.** Binary precision with positive class Yes only works if the evaluation set includes those FP items labeled No (not a detection) or if findings themselves are the Items labeled true/false positive. Do not trust `evaluate accuracy` precision until that set exists.

4. **Existing hooks.** `exhaustiveScopeFiles` on eval cases already feeds local `score.ts` precision. Human adjudication of first exhaustive scope is DATAP-c66199. Ground-truth schema already says: if exhaustive review is incomplete, publish recall and negatives only; label output-derived precision as provisional.

5. **Do not** fold this into the first recall scorecard. Collect design here; file child epics after agreement.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text: Recall-first Plexus path is now DATAP-bd3b69. This initiative stays precision-only.
